segments.source: Roles are defined as follows: Town Council makes local policy and approves the budget; Public Works Office maintains roads; Local Court decides legal disputes; Election Committee administers elections; School Board sets school policies. A resident asks which institution should set school calendar rules.
Rules.
Match the requested action to the stated role. Do not choose an institution merely because it is powerful or familiar.
Task.
Should the request go first to the School Board or the Health Office? Why?
Step-by-step solution.
1. Identify the action: set school calendar rules. 2. Find the role whose definition contains that function: School Board. 3. Health Office has a different stated role, so it is not the first match.
Answer.
The request should go first to the School Board.
Knowledge takeaway.
Institutional reasoning is role matching, not guessing which body is “most important.”
Formal model.
Bipartite relation between actions and authorized institutional roles.
C6. Public budgets and priorities
Problem 616. Choosing a public budget package: case 1
Knowledge context.
Public budgets require choices under limited resources. A transparent model separates costs, benefits, and mandatory obligations.
Given facts.

A town has a budget of 16 units. Projects (cost, benefit): park=(4,5); bridge repair=(6,9); library books=(3,4); drainage=(5,8). Cross-domain check: on a field sketch, 1 cm represents 3 km and two checkpoints are 2 cm apart.
Rules.

Choose a subset whose total cost does not exceed the budget. Maximize total benefit. If a mandatory project is stated, every feasible plan must include it. For the cross-domain check, real distance = sketch distance × kilometres per centimetre.
Task.
Which set of projects gives the greatest total benefit while satisfying every constraint? Cross-domain check: what real distance separates the checkpoints?
Step-by-step solution.

1. Budget limit is 16. 2. Evaluate feasible combinations (and keep the mandatory project if any). 3. The best feasible combination has cost 15 and benefit 22: ['park', 'bridge repair', 'drainage']. 4. No higher-benefit feasible combination exists under the stated costs. Cross-domain check: 2×3=6 km.
Answer.
Choose park, bridge repair, drainage; cost 15, benefit 22. Cross-domain answer: 6 km.
Knowledge takeaway.
Optimization means comparing feasible alternatives under an explicit objective, not simply choosing the cheapest item.
Formal model.
0/1 knapsack with optional mandatory-item constraint; maximize benefit subject to total cost ≤ budget.
Problem 617. Choosing a public budget package: case 2
Knowledge context.
Public budgets require choices under limited resources. A transparent model separates costs, benefits, and mandatory obligations.
Given facts.

A town has a budget of 17 units. Projects (cost, benefit): tree planting=(5,7); bridge repair=(6,9); library books=(3,4); drainage=(5,8). Cross-domain check: a survey team starts work at 8:00 and works for 2 hour(s) without a break.
Rules.

Choose a subset whose total cost does not exceed the budget. Maximize total benefit. If a mandatory project is stated, every feasible plan must include it. For the cross-domain check, finishing time = starting time + duration.
Task.
Which set of projects gives the greatest total benefit while satisfying every constraint? Cross-domain check: at what time does the team finish?
Step-by-step solution.

1. Budget limit is 17. 2. Evaluate feasible combinations (and keep the mandatory project if any). 3. The best feasible combination has cost 16 and benefit 24: ['tree planting', 'bridge repair', 'drainage']. 4. No higher-benefit feasible combination exists under the stated costs. Cross-domain check: 8+2=10, so the team finishes at 10:00.
Answer.
Choose tree planting, bridge repair, drainage; cost 16, benefit 24. Cross-domain answer: 10:00.
Knowledge takeaway.
Optimization means comparing feasible alternatives under an explicit objective, not simply choosing the cheapest item.
Formal model.
0/1 knapsack with optional mandatory-item constraint; maximize benefit subject to total cost ≤ budget.
